### Summary

At the pin there is one gravity-work form, the face form, and on every grid that has an $x_1$ measure for it the
corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork is added automatically. A run with gravity on a Cartesian, spherical-polar or
cubed-sphere grid therefore conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$, not $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$; on a grid with no
measure (`cylindrical`) it conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$. The cycle line logs the matching potential
energy as `pe=`, so `ie=` plus `pe=` is the invariant of the run in both cases.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Says which invariant is exact, per stage, for each grid, and which test is its oracle.

**Data.** The integrated invariants $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ and $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ [J]; the logged `ie=` and `pe=`.

**Placement.** A guide across @sec-ch06-cell to @sec-ch06-vic; it adds no step of its own.

**Activation.** `gravity-work: face` (its only value) with $g_1\ne0$; the grid decides between $P$ and $\mathrm{PE}_d$.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact means to round-off on a closed column; open $x_1$ boundaries change every invariant.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch06-conserves-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathcal E=E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ [J] as a function of the state; $o_i$ [m] the offset of the volume
centroid from the stored centre `x1v`, as in @sec-ch06-dwork.

Every form in this chapter is the identity @eq-ch06-dwork-booked with a different discrete potential energy, so
"what does it conserve" is "which $P$ does it use". The face form uses $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$; the corrected-PE work uses
the fourth-order $P$ of @eq-ch06-dwork-pe. The removed cell form used none and left the defect
@eq-ch06-cell-defect, which the removed fixer repaired once per step (@sec-ch06-cell, @sec-ch06-fixer). An oracle
that checks $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ on a run with the corrected-PE work measures the wrong quantity.

### Derivation

The template @eq-ch06-dwork-booked conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ exactly on a closed column for any $P$. The
stage-by-stage argument extends to the step in three steps:

1. $\mathcal E=E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ is linear in the state, and $\mathcal E(\Delta t\,\mathcal L)=0$ on a closed column by
   @eq-ch06-dwork-booked.
2. A stage gives $\mathcal E(\mathbf U^{\mathrm{new}})=w_0^{(s)}\mathcal E(\mathbf U^n)+w_1^{(s)}\mathcal E(\mathbf U)$, and
   $w_0^{(s)}+w_1^{(s)}=1$ for every stage of the integrators at the pyharp pin, `rk1`, `rk2`, `rk3` and `rk3s4`
   (`IntegratorImpl`, [`pyharp integrator.cpp:33-81`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L33-L81)).
3. By induction over the stages, $\mathcal E(\mathbf U)=\mathcal E(\mathbf U^n)$ after each stage, hence after the step.

It is the unit sum $w_0+w_1=1$ that the argument uses, not convexity. In the implicit solve the matrix part
@eq-ch06-dwork-couple plus the remainder @eq-ch06-dwork-remainder book the work of the mass actually moved, so the
same holds with an implicit scheme. On a `gnomonic-equiangle` grid the stored centre `x1v` is the face midpoint,
not the volume centroid, and the work gains $g_1o_i\dot\rho_i$ (@eq-ch06-dwork-cs); `[C25]` of `derivation_check.py`
checks the step $\phi(x_{1,i})=\phi(x_{1v,i})-g_1o_i$.[^ch06-cons-chk]

    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch06/checks/derivation_check.py`, CPU, double, 1 process;

### Numerical method

@tbl-ch06-conserves-summary is the oracle guide. Exact means to round-off on a closed column (reflecting $x_1$
walls); with an open $x_1$ boundary every invariant changes by the potential-energy flux through it.

| grid | exact invariant | when | logged | oracle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cartesian, spherical-polar, gnomonic-equiangle | $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ | every stage, explicit and VIC | `ie=`+`pe=` ($P$) | `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_python` |
| no $x_1$ measure (`cylindrical`) | $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ | every stage | `ie=`+`pe=` ($\mathrm{PE}_d$) | none at the pin |

: What a run with gravity conserves on a closed column, which logged sum measures it and which test checks it.
The cell form and the fixer are refused at the pin (@sec-ch06-cell, @sec-ch06-fixer). {#tbl-ch06-conserves-summary}

Where the energy is booked: the face form and the corrected-PE term are formed once per stage in
`HydroImpl::forward` as `gravity_energy_correction`, and added to the energy row before the implicit solve when
there is one (@sec-ch06-face, @sec-ch06-dwork); the solve carries the face rows and the corrected-PE rows
(@sec-ch06-vic). At an internal $x_1$ seam the corrected-PE work takes the centred slope of one block, and the
logged $P$ does the same with the exchanged ghost density, so a split column conserves the one-block $P$. A
periodic $x_1$ column keeps one-sided slopes at its block edges and has no single-valued $P$; setup warns.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `face`, the only form | {{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `gravity_work` | `gravity-work` |
| where the corrected-PE work acts | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}} | `radial_exact_work` | none |
| grids with a corrected-PE form | {{< code src/hydro/gravity_work.hpp x1_measure >}} | `x1_measure` | `geometry.type` |
| corrected-PE work, seams | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `corrected_pe_work_seam` | none |
| $\mathrm{PE}_d$ or $P$ summed and printed as `pe=` | {{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp print_cycle_line >}} | `pe_sum` | none |

: Code map of where the gravity work is booked and where the logged sums are formed. {#tbl-ch06-conserves-code}

`print_cycle_line` sums `pe` as $\rho\phi$ at `x1v`, minus `corrected_pe_work_seam` of the density when
`radial_exact_work` holds, and prints it as `pe=`; so `pe=` is $P$ under the corrected-PE work and $\mathrm{PE}_d$
otherwise. The cycle line has no fixer field.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_python` | per-step $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$, explicit and VIC, on Cartesian, spherical-polar and gnomonic-equiangle columns and a 2-D box | $10^{-14}$ rel. | `EP_TOL` |
| `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_python` | the logged `ie=`+`pe=` equals the test's $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ | $10^{-11}$ | `DIAG_TOL` |
| `test_x1_seam_split_radial_exact.release` | 2 vs 1 $x_1$ blocks: state gap and the split $E+P$ drift | $10^{-13}$ both | `EXPECT_LE` |
| `test_implicit_face_work_operator_python` | the tall column's $E+P$ drift under VIC | $10^{-11}$ | `EPE_TOL` |

: Oracles of each grid's invariant. {#tbl-ch06-conserves-tests}

The tolerances are module constants of {{< code tests/test_gravity_work_radial_exact.py >}} and
{{< code tests/test_implicit_face_work_operator.py >}}. At the pin the ctests of the table pass.[^ch06-cons-run]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
On a run with the corrected-PE work every $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ check measures the wrong invariant: check
`ie=`+`pe=`. No ctest at the pin checks the invariant of a `cylindrical` run.
:::

- The six-panel cubed-sphere conservation numbers of the development round were measured off the pin; no ctest at
  the pin asserts $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ across panel seams.
- Combinations with the study switches: @sec-ch12-matrix.
